title: Recovering joint kinetics from motion: inverse dynamics on real WBDS walking, validated against the dataset's own moments

dataset.name: A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics (WBDS)
dataset.record: 5 adults (WBDS01-05), self-selected-speed treadmill walking (walkT05); marker trajectories (mkr) + ground reaction force (grf) as inputs, and the dataset's own inverse-dynamics joint moments (knt) as the validation reference; right-limb sagittal ankle/knee/hip
dataset.citation: Fukuchi CA, Fukuchi RK, Duarte M. A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics in healthy individuals. PeerJ 2018;6:e4640; data figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.5722711 (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: Motion capture measures how the body MOVES (kinematics); the clinically decisive quantities are the joint MOMENTS that cause the motion (kinetics), and inverse dynamics is how you get from one to the other. Driving the ecosystem's 2-D Newton-Euler inverse dynamics with real WBDS markers + ground reaction force -- and validating against the dataset's OWN independently-computed joint moments -- the recovered sagittal moments agree strongly and, revealingly, with a DISTAL-TO-PROXIMAL accuracy gradient: ankle r = 0.97, knee r = 0.85, hip r = 0.77 (mean over 5 subjects). The ankle (nearest the measured GRF) is recovered almost exactly, including the ~1.5-1.7 N·m/kg push-off plantarflexor peak; the hip degrades and its peak inflates -- the textbook error-propagation of inverse dynamics up the kinematic chain, here compounded by the greater-trochanter hip-centre proxy. The case reproduces a real methodological truth, not just a number.

claims.statement: mean correlation of the recovered sagittal ANKLE moment with the WBDS reference moment (5 subjects)
mean correlation of the recovered sagittal KNEE moment with the reference (5 subjects)
mean correlation of the recovered sagittal HIP moment with the reference (5 subjects; degrades proximally)
reference ankle plantarflexor push-off peak, body-mass-normalised (N·m/kg)

validation.reference: The WBDS distribution provides its OWN inverse-dynamics joint moments (knt files, computed by the dataset authors' independent pipeline) -- a real, external ground truth. A correct inverse-dynamics implementation must (1) recover the sagittal moment WAVEFORMS (high correlation), most accurately at the ankle (closest to the measured GRF); (2) recover the physiological ankle plantarflexor push-off peak magnitude (~1.5-1.7 N·m/kg); and (3) exhibit the known distal-to-proximal accuracy degradation of inverse dynamics -- which the ecosystem reproduces (ankle 0.97 > knee 0.85 > hip 0.77).
validation.data: REAL -- Fukuchi et al. 2018 (figshare 5722711), 5 subjects, 3D motion capture + force-plate treadmill; inputs = markers + GRF, reference = the dataset's own knt joint moments
validation.note: The reproducible finding is that the ecosystem's Newton-Euler inverse dynamics recovers walking joint kinetics from real kinematics + GRF, validated against the dataset's OWN moments, with the expected distal-to-proximal accuracy gradient (ankle r=0.973, knee r=0.847, hip r=0.774 over 5 subjects). HONEST scope: (1) the recovered moment SIGN is a per-joint convention (extensor/flexor); agreement is on the sign-aligned waveform (|r|) and peak magnitude. (2) 2-D SAGITTAL analysis only -- WBDS's own moments are 3-D; the frontal/transverse components are out of scope. (3) The HIP degrades (r=0.77) and its peak INFLATES (recovered ~1.46 vs reference ~0.93 N·m/kg) because the greater-trochanter marker is a crude proxy for the true (medial) hip joint centre and inverse-dynamics error accumulates up the chain -- this is a real, documented limitation, reported not hidden. (4) The right belt = the right foot was confirmed empirically (its GRF gives the physically-consistent ankle moment, r=0.97); WBDS treadmill trials carry no force-plate-foot assignment.

open_questions.q: A functional hip-joint-centre estimate (from the pelvis markers) instead of the greater-trochanter proxy, and a full 3-D inverse dynamics (frontal/transverse moments), would tighten the proximal agreement; an OpenSim residual-reduction / static-optimisation pass (PhysioOpenSim) would push toward muscle-level kinetics. Documented, not escalated.
